greeting.text: *looks up from coiling a rope* Well now, a face I don't know! Come to book passage, or just come to admire the finest hull ever to cross these waters? *pats the boat's side*

choices.text: I'm looking for a ride. Where are you sailing to?

destination.text: Depends who's paying and how the wind's feeling! Regular run takes me down past Catraniz, and I've put in at Sit Nalta more times than I can count - though don't ask me to count, arithmetic was never my trade. *grins* Where's it you're headed?

choices.text: Wherever you want to take me. I don't have much to trade. What do you ask in return?

payment.text: *waves a hand* Lazulis are nice, sure, but I've hauled men across for nothing more than a good story I hadn't heard before. Mind you, I've heard most of them twice over - I read, you see, more than a sailor ought to. *taps his temple* So tell me something worth the passage, and we'll call it settled.

choices.text: I heard someone sailed south to a new continent and never came back. Their siblings are organizing a search, leaving from a highway's southern end. I heard this in Khol Moshin - know anything about it?

darnis_reveal.text: *sits up straight, all trader-charm dropped* Därnis! That's the name you're circling round, unless I miss my guess - sailed south out of Sindäara and came back changed, talking of a new ocean, a burning island, land that floated. Historians took that as a sign there was a whole continent down there waiting. But siblings chasing after him, a highway running clean to the southern tip - that part's new to me, and I won't pretend otherwise. Khol Moshin's a fair place to hear it, mind. Lot of talk passes through there I never catch.

choices.text: Guess it's off the beaten path for a wise sailman like you - nowhere near the coast. Have you been there?

khol_moshin_no.text: *laughs, waving it off* Been there? Man, I've got sea legs, not mountain boots - if there's no coastline, I've got no business there. I know the name, know the trains run through it, but Khol Moshin's someone else's country to walk, not mine.

choices.text: Makes sense. So you said Därnis made it back? I thought he'd gone missing. Where did you hear this?

ensayo_source.text: Read it, not heard it - I've got an old copy of the Ensayo, era nine and all. Way it's written, aye, he came back long enough to tell of it: the new ocean, the burning island, land that floated on the water like it hadn't decided to be land yet. *shrugs* What happened to him after that telling, the book doesn't say - and I've learned not to trust a chronicle to finish a story just because it started one.

choices.text: Ensayo? What's that? I haven't heard of it.

ensayo_explain.text: Ensayo - full history of the world, near as anyone's bothered to write one, era by era, dated by this Vortex-reckoning folk use here. Only thing is, it's not the only one - there's a Libro too, tells the same stretch of years its own way, different names for the eras, different lines drawn between them, and neither book so much as nods at the other. *spreads hands* I've read both. Doesn't make me any wiser on which one's lying - could be neither, far as I know, just two men who never compared notes.

choices.text: And where did you find these books? Are they accessible to anyone?

bracco_intro.text: *scratches beard* Mine own copies, traded off a fella in Gorff years back - paid more in fish than I'd like to admit. Whether there's some proper library holding the 'real' ones, official-like, anyone could just walk into? Couldn't tell you. Never gone looking myself - a sailor reads what falls in his lap, not what he has to hunt for.

choices.text: Remember the name of that fella? Or what they looked like at least?

bracco_desc.text: *thinking* Called himself Bracco, or Braggo - something like that, I never trust a name a stranger gives twice the same way. Big fella, more scars than a proper trader ought to have, sold me the books like he wanted rid of them more than he wanted my lazulis. *shrugs* Didn't ask questions. Man selling cheap history isn't a man you interrogate.

choices.text: Bracco. Interesting. Any idea where he was coming from, or where he was going?

bracco_unknown.text: Not a clue, truth told. He wasn't the talking kind - paid, took my fish, walked off toward the docks and I never saw which boat he took, or if he even had one. *taps table* For all I know he swam. Man like that, wouldn't put it past him.

choices.text: Thank you. I think I'll stick around a bit longer - I'd like to know more about this Bracco.

farewell.text: *tips an imaginary hat* Suit yourself - this dock isn't going anywhere, and neither am I till the tide turns proper. Ask around, someone'll point you the right way if Bracco's still working these parts. And hey - if you find him, tell him his book cost me a week's catch. I'd like that on record somewhere.
